head.h1: Finger Food Catering in Dubai — Real Prices, Menus and Timings

opening_paragraph: Finger food catering in Dubai from myCHEF starts at AED 150 per person for a passed canape reception, or AED 90 for drop-off trays. Handheld sliders, skewers and sharing boards are cooked and served by a vetted chef, so your guests graze while you host. It suits any room where people are standing, drink in hand, moving between conversations instead of sitting down to a plated dinner. You tell us the headcount, the venue and the mood; we design the menu, bring the chef and service team, run the party and clear it all away. Below you will find what is included, the menu options, honest prices and how to hire the right team for your event.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What does finger food catering include?
new_paragraphs: Finger food catering includes the whole job, from the first menu conversation to the last tray cleared — not just a box of bites left at your door. A typical booking covers menu design, a vetted chef and service team, all the food and its preparation, delivery and on-site setup, plus cleanup where the format calls for it. As the team coordinating your booking, we also handle the practical layer most people forget: platters and stands, chafing dishes or induction stations for anything served hot, serviettes, and enough hands to keep trays circulating. A drop-off caterer will deliver finished platters ready to lay out, which keeps the cost down for a relaxed gathering. A full-service booking adds chefs finishing bites on site and waiters passing them, which is what you want when you would sooner greet guests than plate canapés. We size every one of those services to your headcount and space.

replace_in_block.new_heading: How much does finger food catering cost in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Finger food catering in Dubai costs from AED 150 per person for a passed canape reception, and the final figure moves with headcount, menu and how it is served. Drop-off trays laid out by you are our least expensive route at AED 90 a head. Live stations sit at AED 150 and are quoted with their own chef on top. Plated private-chef service, where the same bites are finished and served course by course, runs AED 700 to AED 950. Set catering packages start at AED 1,200 and scale to AED 2,400 and beyond as courses, stations and staffing are added.
The finger food catering price list, in full
People ask for a price list and usually get a "contact us", so here is ours in one place. Everything below is per person unless it says otherwise, and 5% VAT is added to the total.
Drop-off trays — finished platters delivered ready to lay out, no staff on site: from AED 90 .
Buffet-style spread — laid out and maintained by a service team: from AED 120 .
Passed canape reception — waiters circulating trays, chefs finishing hot bites on site: from AED 150 .
Live and interactive stations — from AED 150 , with each station quoted as its own unit including its chef.
Plated private-chef service — AED 700 to AED 950 , where a chef cooks and plates for a seated table.
Set packages — AED 1,200 , 2,400 , 3,600 , 4,500 and 5,500 , each covering a defined menu and guest band.
Minimums — 10 guests on volume formats, 20 on a buffet, and a minimum order of AED 900 .

There is no per-piece rate, and any caterer quoting one is guessing at your guest count for you. Work it the other way instead: take 8 to 12 pieces per guest for a two-hour reception, multiply by your headcount, and the per-head tier already covers that quantity. Grazing tables, rentals and extra staff are separate lines on the quote, never folded into the per-head figure. Our Dubai catering price guide breaks down what moves each number.

add_block.new_heading: Finger food catering for weddings, corporate events and parties
new_paragraphs: Finger food works for almost any occasion because it keeps a room moving — nobody is anchored to a seat, so guests mingle. For weddings and engagements, passed bites during the drinks reception bridge the gap between the ceremony and the seated meal. Corporate finger food catering fits launches, office celebrations and networking evenings, where people need to eat one-handed while they talk business; we can run a discreet, branded service that scales from a boardroom to a ballroom. For birthdays, house parties and pool days, finger food party catering is the quickest way to feed a crowd well without a formal sit-down. It is equally at home as finger food catering for events on a rooftop, in a villa garden or on a yacht. Whatever the setting, the menu and the number of staff flex to match the guest count and the pace you want the evening to keep.

Choose a few arrival nibbles for the tables, then cold bites for the first hour, hot bites as the room fills, and something sweet to close. Cheap finger food catering, honestly defined, is the drop-off version of this same list: trays delivered ready to lay out, with no chefs or waiters on site, so the labour comes out of the quote. A station sells the theatre as much as the food, and each one is quoted with its own chef. Which of them travels to you is decided by the address, and it is worth knowing the answer before the menu is signed.

Interactive hot pot: guests cook their own proteins, vegetables, noodles and rice in shared broths.
Sliders station: beef, chicken, mushroom and vegetarian, griddled to order.

At a villa the fired stations run as written, outdoors on your own plot: the robata and charcoal grill, the pizza oven and the shawarma spit all sit on the driveway, garden or hard standing. The line Dubai Municipality draws is enclosure — "do not light coal in an enclosed space or indoors" — and the UAE Fire Code keeps gas cylinders at ground level and off roofs and terraces (Table 11.1). In an apartment or tower none of them go up. Emaar's vertical-community rules prohibit "barbecues, grills, or any cooking equipment of any kind" on balconies and terraces whatever the fuel, and no LPG cylinder may be brought into the building, so the robata becomes an electric yakitori griddle, the shawarma an electric spit, and the carvery runs untouched because it carries no heat source at all.

On a yacht the cylinder is the deciding clause: no extra gas bottle may be kept aboard (D-Marin Art. 53.1(a)) and Dubai Harbour bans operating gas cylinders and live fire on marina premises (section 7.4). The shawarma spit and the gas pizza oven stay ashore; the carvery, the sushi counter, the hot pot and induction-griddled sliders come aboard, and where the boat has its own fitted grill the crew runs it while our chef preps and passes. On an open public beach a fire outside a designated zone is a Dubai Municipality offence carrying a Dh500 fine, so the reception is carried by the carvery, the sushi counter and the cold canapes; a permitted private event or a licensed beach club brings the fired stations back with the permit stack behind them. For a rooftop or a desert site we put the setup to the building or the site operator and confirm it before quoting.

The fried bites are the one family that seldom fries live at a private address. Loukoumades, croquettes, samosas, tempura and calamari all want open hot oil, and open hot oil wants a grease-rated hood with suppression that homes, towers and boats do not carry. They are fried in a licensed partner kitchen, carried hot and crisped to order at the pass on site, so they reach the tray crisp instead of steaming under a cloche. Nothing comes off the list above; it is fried in a different room.

A grazing table is an install rather than a delivery: boards, risers, linen and garnish are styled on site around the guest count, and it doubles as the centrepiece of the room before anyone touches it.

The canape builder: one base plus one filling

new_paragraphs: Plan roughly 8 to 12 pieces per guest for a two-hour reception, and more when the bites stand in for a full meal instead of accompanying it. Styling then follows the room: trays passed by waiters keep a formal event elegant and controlled; a laid-out spread or grazing table suits a warmer, help-yourself party; and live stations turn the food itself into entertainment. Timing matters as much as quantity — bites are staggered so hot items arrive hot and the table does not look picked-over halfway through. For outdoor and poolside events we plan for Dubai's climate, keeping cold items chilled and hot items finished on site. Tell us the length of the event and the feel you are after, and the menu, the pieces per head and the service style are all sized to fit.

new_paragraphs: To hire finger food catering, send us your headcount, venue and date, and we return an itemised proposal — usually within one business day. From there it is four simple steps. First, we agree the menu, the pieces per guest and the service style. Second, we confirm the chef and lock the quote, with no surprise line items later. Third, on the day the team arrives ahead of guests to set up, whether that is a home catering delivery to your villa or a full brigade for a corporate floor. Fourth, they serve, replenish and clear, leaving your kitchen the way they found it. Because the partner kitchens and chefs we work with are licensed in Dubai and operate within local food-safety rules, the same booking covers a quiet dinner for eight or a launch for two hundred. new_paragraphs: MyCHEF was founded by a chef trained in some of Europe's most demanding kitchens, on one idea: you own the evening, we carry the work. MyCHEF is implementing a 12-stage partner verification framework covering identity, trade licence, permitted activities, food-safety documentation and references; the partner assigned to your booking is checked against the stages that apply to the services it performs. We are honest about it, too: no system removes every risk, so we match each event to the best available chef for it.

For a finger food reception that leans Italian and Mediterranean, that is often Marco Rossi , whose small-plate and sharing-board background makes him a natural fit for handheld menus and live stations; for a classic, fine-dining edge we may bring in Ahmed Al-Rashid instead. Alongside finger food catering we have delivered villa weddings, yacht celebrations and corporate galas in Dubai. Real client reviews for Finger food catering are published as events happen.

Do you publish a finger food catering price list?

Yes, in full on this page: AED 90 drop-off, AED 120 buffet-style, AED 150 passed canapes and live stations, AED 700 to AED 950 plated. There is no per-piece rate — plan 8 to 12 pieces per guest for two hours and the per-head tier covers that quantity. Rentals and extra staff are separate lines.
What's included in finger food catering?

Included are menu design, a vetted chef and service team, the food and its preparation, delivery and setup, and cleanup where relevant. Platters, stands and staffing scale to your headcount and venue.
How many finger food pieces should I plan per guest?
Plan 8 to 12 pieces per guest for a two-hour party, and more if the bites replace a meal. We size the menu and the number of staff to your event's length and pace.

Yes. Menus are halal by default in Dubai, and every board can be built vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free or nut-free without a separate charge for the substitution.

Affordable options start with a passed, drop-off spread, while luxury service with chefs and waiters sits higher. We deliver to every neighbourhood in Dubai, so the service comes to your address.
How do I hire finger food catering?
Hiring is clear: share your headcount, venue and schedule, and we send an itemised proposal, usually within one business day, then confirm the chef and menu once you approve.
Can you cater corporate finger food events and large parties?
Yes. Corporate finger food catering, product launches and private parties of any size are all covered, with live stations or passed trays and staff scaled to the guest count.

add_block.new_heading: What's on a finger food menu?
new_paragraphs: A finger food menu is built from three families — hot bites, cold bites and something sweet — then tuned to your cuisine and dietary needs. Hot options run from mini sliders, spiced chicken skewers and arancini to koftas and crisp spring rolls; cold options cover sushi, bruschetta, ceviche spoons and mezze. Grazing and sharing boards anchor the table with cheeses, cured and grilled meats, dips and warm bread, and a private finger food chef can plate a live station — carving, sushi or a hot-off-the-pan bite — as a centrepiece. Cuisine is yours to choose: Arabic and Levantine mezze, Italian and Mediterranean small plates, pan-Asian, or modern Indian. Every menu is halal by default in Dubai, and any board can be built vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free or nut-free without a surcharge for the substitution. Sweet finger desserts — mini tarts, macarons and fruit skewers — round off the spread.
